title: How do you make an existing List immutable?
shortTitle: How do you make an existing List immutable?
keyPoints: List.of(a, b, c) creates a truly immutable list (Java 9+)
Collections.unmodifiableList(list) creates a VIEW – the original can still be modified!
Any add/remove/set on an immutable list throws UnsupportedOperationException
Understanding this concept is essential for Java interviews at senior level

s1_definition.oneliner: List.of() and List.copyOf() create truly immutable lists. Collections.unmodifiableList() is only an unmodifiable view – the underlying list can still change.
s1_definition.profdef:
Three approaches:

- **List.of(a, b, c)** – truly immutable. No null elements allowed. Throws on modification.
- **List.copyOf(list)** – copies the list into an immutable version. Modifications to the original do not affect the copy.
- **Collections.unmodifiableList(list)** – wraps the original. Prevents modification through the wrapper, but the original list can still be modified, and the wrapper reflects those changes.
s1_definition.analogy: List.of is a printed, laminated bank statement – truly unmodifiable. Collections.unmodifiableList is a glass cover over the original statement – you cannot write on it, but someone with access to the original underneath can still change it.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  List.of("A", "B")            → immutable, independent
  List.copyOf(mutableList)     → immutable copy, independent
  Collections.unmodifiableList → read-only VIEW of the original (not independent!)

  Any modification → UnsupportedOperationException
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Use List.of() or List.copyOf() for truly immutable lists. Collections.unmodifiableList() is only a view – modifications to the underlying list are still visible through it.

One sentence to remember: List.of() is truly immutable, Collections.unmodifiableList is just a read-only view over a still-mutable list.
